info.name: mtel-skill-resolver (MCP)
info.description:
Manual testing for the mtel-skill-resolver MCP server over its Streamable HTTP transport (resolver/http.js).

Start the server first:
    cd resolver && PORT=3939 npm run start:http

Then adjust the `baseUrl` collection variable if you used a different port.

KEY GOTCHAS
- The /mcp endpoint REQUIRES `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream`. Without text/event-stream you get 406 Not Acceptable.
- Responses come back as Server-Sent Events (text/event-stream), not plain JSON. The payload is on the `data:` line, and the matched skills are JSON stringified inside result.content[0].text (double-encoded, an MCP convention). The test scripts below parse both layers and log the result to the Postman Console (View > Show Postman Console).
- If you start the server with MCP_AUTH_TOKEN set, put that value in the `authToken` variable and enable the Authorization header on the /mcp requests.

request.description: Plain REST liveness probe (not MCP). Expects {"status":"ok",...}. Stays open even when MCP_AUTH_TOKEN is set.

header.description: Enable only if the server was started with MCP_AUTH_TOKEN (the bundle is gated the same as /mcp).

request.description: Static skill catalog: metadata + each skill's full markdown body. Plain JSON (not SSE). A client can fetch this once and let the user pick which skills to write into .claude/skills/ without cloning the registry. 404s until `npm run build` has generated bundle.json.

exec: // The MCP Streamable HTTP transport replies with SSE. Pull the JSON off the `data:` line.
pm.test('got an SSE data line', () => pm.expect(dataLine, 'no data: line in response').to.be.a('string'));

header.description: Enable only if the server was started with MCP_AUTH_TOKEN.

request.description: Lists the tools the server exposes, with their input JSON-Schema. This is what an MCP client reads to know resolve_skills exists and what arguments it takes.

exec: // Parse the two encoding layers: SSE data: line -> JSON-RPC -> stringified tool text.
pm.test('got an SSE data line', () => pm.expect(dataLine, 'no data: line in response').to.be.a('string'));
const text = rpc.result && rpc.result.content && rpc.result.content[0] && rpc.result.content[0].text;
pm.test('tool returned text content', () => pm.expect(text, 'no content[0].text').to.be.a('string'));

header.description: Enable only if the server was started with MCP_AUTH_TOKEN.

request.description: Calls the resolve_skills tool. Edit the `keywords` array in the body to try different stacks. Transitive requires are pulled in automatically (e.g. nextjs -> react, supabase -> postgres). The parsed result is logged to the Postman Console.
